problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=2,{x}_{2}={x}_{3}=4,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-5.$ Find $P(x).$
worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}={x}_{3}=4,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-5,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =-5(x-2)(x-4)(x-4) \\  & =-5(x-2)(x-4)(x-4)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-5(x-2)(x-4)(x-4) & =-5({x}^{2}-6x+8)(x-4) \\  & =-5({x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}-6{x}^{2}+24x+8x-32) \\  & =-5({x}^{3}-10{x}^{2}+32x-32) \\  & =-5{x}^{3}+50{x}^{2}-160x+160.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-5{x}^{3}+50{x}^{2}-160x+160.$
